text: The Taliban has released a new biography of founder Mullah Mohammed Omar to dispel rumors of his death. The document asserts Omar remains the movement's leader and aims to reinforce his leadership credentials amid the rise of ISIS.

Hundreds gathered in Summerville, S.C., Saturday for the funeral of Walter Scott, who was fatally shot by a police officer. Mourners described the Coast Guard veteran's death as a catalyst for racial justice reform. Officer Michael Slager faces murder charges following the release of bystander video showing the shooting.

A former TSA agent was sentenced to six months in jail and five and a half years of probation for secretly filming a female co-worker in a restroom. Investigators also discovered more than 1,500 photos and 90 videos of the victim taken inside her home. Daniel Boykin pleaded guilty to unlawful photography, aggravated burglary, and computer act violations.

Cape Verde is leveraging its rich musical heritage to drive economic growth and boost tourism. Through initiatives like the Kriol Jazz Festival and the Atlantic Music Expo, the nation aims to transform its creative sector into a major global export.

Arsenal kept Premier League title hopes alive with a 1-0 win over Burnley, fueled by an Aaron Ramsey goal. The victory moves the club within four points of leaders Chelsea ahead of their upcoming head-to-head clash. Elsewhere, Aston Villa defeated Tottenham 1-0, while Crystal Palace secured a 4-1 win over Sunderland.

Original *Twin Peaks* cast members have launched a #SaveTwinPeaks campaign to support David Lynch following his exit from the Showtime revival due to a salary dispute. The actors released a video backing Lynch, who cited insufficient funding to execute his creative vision. Showtime stated it remains hopeful to proceed with both creators at the helm.

Andrew Getty, 47, grandson of oil tycoon J. Paul Getty, has died of natural causes. LAPD reports no foul play is suspected and no criminal investigation is underway. An autopsy is pending to determine the exact cause of death.

Maryland police say Nyia Parler cannot be extradited to Philadelphia to face charges for abandoning her quadriplegic son in the woods until she completes an unspecified treatment. Parler was arrested in Montgomery County after allegedly leaving the 21-year-old in a park for four days to visit a boyfriend. The victim is currently receiving medical treatment for dehydration and malnutrition.

NASA astrophysicist Amy Mainzer has named asteroid 316201 after Nobel Peace Prize winner and education activist Malala Yousafzai. The 4-kilometer-wide asteroid orbits the sun between Mars and Jupiter. Mainzer honored Yousafzai to recognize her contributions and address the underrepresentation of women in asteroid naming.

A gastrointestinal illness has affected 100 passengers and crew members aboard the Celebrity Infinity cruise ship. The CDC is investigating the cause and will meet the vessel in San Diego on Monday. Celebrity Cruises has increased disinfection procedures and is collecting specimens for testing.

Weekly trending stories include the surprise digital HD release of the "Star Wars" saga and Nina Dobrev's departure from "The Vampire Diaries." Mindy Kaling's brother faces backlash over claims of faking his race for medical school, while fans mourn the death of "Dukes of Hazzard" actor James Best.

The FBI charged a Philadelphia woman with attempting to travel to Turkey to join ISIS. Two New York women were also arrested this week for allegedly planning to build explosive devices for domestic attacks.

HBO has released a teaser for the second season of "True Detective," set to premiere June 21. The new installment stars Colin Farrell, Vince Vaughn, Rachel McAdams, and Taylor Kitsch in a California-based conspiracy investigation.

Carlos Colina, 32, has been charged with assault and improper disposal of a body following the discovery of human remains in a duffel bag in Cambridge, Massachusetts. Authorities identified the victim as 26-year-old Jonathan Camilien, an acquaintance of Colina. Investigations are ongoing to determine if additional charges are warranted.

Louisville high school basketball recruit Trey Moses has gone viral after asking Ellie Meredith, a freshman with Down syndrome, to be his prom date. The gesture, which included a Taylor Swift-themed "prom-posal," was facilitated through the school's Best Buddies program. Moses plans to study special education at Ball State University next year.

NBC debuts "A.D. The Bible Continues" this Sunday, a 12-week miniseries following the early days of Christianity. Other notable upcoming releases include the final episodes of AMC's "Mad Men" and the premiere of Netflix's "Marvel's Daredevil."

Indiana Governor Mike Pence's signing of a controversial religious freedom law is seen as a move to bolster his conservative credentials for a potential 2016 presidential run. The decision has sparked significant backlash and threatens to pull the entire Republican primary field toward more hardline stances on LGBT rights.

Apple has released a mobile OS update featuring increased emoji diversity, including various skin tones and same-sex couple options. The expansion has drawn both praise for inclusivity and criticism from conservative commentators. The update also includes new flag representations, such as the Palestinian flag.

Avril Lavigne revealed to People magazine that she was bedridden for five months after contracting Lyme disease. The singer, who attributed her absence to the illness, stated she is now "80 percent better" and preparing to release a new single.

New research from the Anne Frank House suggests Anne and Margot Frank died at least a month earlier than previously recorded. Re-examination of archives and survivor testimonies indicates the sisters likely succumbed to typhus before February 1945, contradicting earlier Dutch official records.

Two Troy University students were arrested in Florida for the alleged gang rape of a woman during spring break. The suspects, Ryan Calhoun and Delonte Martistee, were identified via video footage discovered during an unrelated investigation. Both men have been suspended from the university pending further arrests.

A stray dog in Washington State survived being hit by a car, struck with a hammer, and buried in a field. The dog, now named Theia, was discovered alive four days later and is receiving medical treatment at Washington State University. Fundraising efforts for her extensive surgeries have already exceeded $10,000.

The FBI confirmed Malaysian bomb maker Zulkifli bin Hir, alias Marwan, was killed during a January raid in the Philippines. Forensic testing verified the identity of the terrorist, who was removed from the FBI's Most Wanted list. The mission resulted in the deaths of 44 Philippine police officers and sparked controversy over a damaged peace agreement.

Critics argue the Obama administration's proposed nuclear framework with Iran grants Tehran excessive concessions while providing insufficient safeguards against cheating. The deal reportedly allows Iran to maintain nuclear infrastructure and receive billions in sanctions relief, potentially funding regional terrorism. Opponents warn the agreement fails to ensure long-term verifiable constraints on Iran's nuclear capabilities.

AMC series "Mad Men" prepares to air its final season this Sunday. Creator Matthew Weiner faces scrutiny over the series' conclusion as the narrative shifts toward the end of the 1960s. Speculation remains high regarding character fates and the show's ultimate thematic resolution.

A giraffe named Katie gave birth to a calf at the Dallas Zoo on Friday evening. The birth was broadcast live via an hour-long Animal Planet stream. The newborn appeared to be in good condition and was seen attempting to stand and nurse.

Loretta Lynch's historic nomination to become the first African-American woman attorney general faces unprecedented delays in the Senate. Supporters cite racial bias for the six-month stalemate, while Republicans attribute the delay to partisan battles over immigration and human trafficking.

Three people were killed and five wounded after armed assailants stormed an attorney general's office in northern Afghanistan's Balkh province on Thursday. Security forces are engaged in an ongoing exchange of fire with the attackers to rescue remaining staff and civilians.

Bob Barker made a guest appearance on "The Price Is Right" on April 1, marking his first return to the show in eight years. The 91-year-old former host guest-hosted the "Lucky Seven" game before returning duties to Drew Carey.
Blues legend B.B. King has been released from the hospital following treatment for dehydration caused by Type II diabetes. The 89-year-old musician is reportedly resting at home.

Dzhokhar Tsarnaev has been found guilty on all counts in the Boston Marathon bombing. The verdict highlights the need to address radicalization by understanding the political and social grievances that extremists exploit. Experts argue that combating violence requires engaging young Muslims through constructive community action rather than religious reformation.

CNN highlights the week's top videos, including a tour of Mike Tyson's former Ohio mansion and footage of the world's tallest giga-coaster. Features also include an exclusive interview regarding sexual assault allegations against yoga leader Bikram Choudhury and a witness account of the Germanwings Flight 9525 crash.

Pentagon maps show coalition forces have reclaimed 25-30% of Iraqi territory previously held by ISIS. Experts warn that while territorial gains are significant, ISIS is likely using asymmetric attacks to distract from conventional losses.

A passenger on an Air Canada flight from Toronto to Atlanta reported being choked with a headphone cord by a stranger during descent. U.S. authorities met the aircraft upon landing, and the suspect was transported for medical and mental evaluation. The FBI is reviewing the incident, though no federal charges are currently pending.

A Hong Kong court has adjourned the murder trial of former banker Rurik Jutting until May to allow for forensic analysis. Jutting faces two counts of murder following the discovery of two Indonesian women's bodies at his Wan Chai apartment last November.

A series of tornadoes swept through the rural Midwest on Thursday, leaving one person dead in Fairdale, Illinois. The storms caused significant property damage across Illinois, Iowa, and Missouri, destroying numerous homes and businesses. Emergency responders continue to assess damage in areas where debris has blocked access to trapped residents.

Don McLean's original manuscript for "American Pie" sold for $1.2 million at a Christie's auction Tuesday. The 16-page draft includes extensive notes and lines omitted from the final version. The sale marks the third-highest price ever achieved for an American literary manuscript.

UNRWA Commissioner-General Pierre Krähenbühl will conduct an emergency visit to Syria's Yarmouk refugee camp on Saturday to assess the humanitarian crisis. The mission aims to address safety concerns for 18,000 remaining residents amid ongoing conflict and severe aid shortages. Krähenbühl will meet with Syrian officials and displaced persons to discuss relief efforts.

Saudi-led coalition airstrikes against Houthi targets in Yemen have killed an estimated 600 people and caused widespread infrastructure collapse. The ICRC is calling for an urgent humanitarian ceasefire as millions face shortages of electricity and clean water. UN Security Council discussions on a ceasefire resolution have so far yielded no decision.

Former Australian cricket captain and legendary broadcaster Richie Benaud has died at age 84. Benaud, a record-breaking leg-spinner and iconic commentator, was widely regarded as one of the game's most influential figures.

A total lunar eclipse, the shortest of the century, began early morning Pacific time across western North America and parts of Asia. The four-minute event is the third in a series of four consecutive eclipses known as a tetrad. Visibility is limited on the U.S. East Coast due to sunrise.

A federal grand jury has charged real estate heir Robert Durst with unlawful possession of a firearm following a hotel room search. The indictment follows recent first-degree murder charges in Los Angeles and various state-level weapons and drug charges in Louisiana. Durst remains held without bail pending extradition.

"Furious 7" premieres Friday, serving as a tribute to late actor Paul Walker following his death in a 2013 car crash. Producers rewrote the script and used body doubles to complete the film without killing off Walker's character. Co-stars and fans continue to honor the actor's legacy ahead of the release.
A model accidentally revealed the correct price of a Hyundai Sonata during a Thursday episode of "The Price Is Right." Host Drew Carey joked about the error as the contestant won the vehicle.

Thai Smile has unveiled a new Airbus A320 featuring a custom "Adventure Time" livery and themed interior. The aircraft, a result of a partnership with Cartoon Network Amazone, will begin service on April 4 on the Bangkok-Phuket route.

Pedestrians in Washington, D.C., intervened Tuesday to safely guide a brood of ducklings across a heavily trafficked street. Bystanders used umbrellas and stopped traffic to corral the birds and move them to a nearby grassy area.

French investigators have completed evidence collection at the Germanwings Flight 9525 crash site in the Alps. Both black boxes have been recovered, and authorities have identified 150 DNA profiles from the wreckage. Preliminary data suggests the co-pilot intentionally crashed the aircraft.

Cuba attends the Summit of the Americas in Panama for the first time since 1962 following a thaw in relations with the U.S. Negotiations continue regarding the reopening of embassies and Cuba's removal from the U.S. state sponsor of terrorism list. Tensions remain high over U.S. policy toward Venezuela and physical clashes between Cuban dissidents and government supporters in Panama.

New Testament accounts suggest Jesus and his disciples relied on donations and hospitality to fund their itinerant ministry. Scholars note that wealthy followers, including women like Mary Magdalene and Joanna, provided essential financial resources to sustain the group.

California regulators ordered PG&E to pay a record $1.6 billion penalty for unsafe gas system operations following the 2010 San Bruno pipeline explosion. Most of the fine is earmarked for mandatory pipeline safety infrastructure improvements.

Lauren Hill, the college basketball player who gained international fame for playing despite terminal brain cancer, has died at age 19. Hill raised $1.4 million for pediatric cancer research and became a global symbol of perseverance.

A massive four-alarm fire broke out Friday morning at the General Electric Appliance Park in Louisville, Kentucky. Thick smoke and flames were reported at the industrial site, though authorities report no injuries or trapped individuals. The cause of the blaze remains unknown.

Iranian Foreign Minister Mohammad Javad Zarif is working to finalize a nuclear deal with U.S. Secretary of State John Kerry ahead of a June 30 deadline. Despite his polished diplomatic image, Zarif's background includes U.S. education, past involvement in student protests, and a previous federal investigation into a foundation linked to Iranian interests.

A Connecticut judge denied a motion to release a 17-year-old girl from state custody following her chemotherapy treatment for Hodgkin lymphoma. Despite being in remission, the teen remains in hospital custody due to concerns from the Department of Children and Families regarding her status as a flight risk. Attorneys for the girl and her mother are considering an appeal.

New computational research suggests the play "Double Falsehood" was written by William Shakespeare and John Fletcher rather than Lewis Theobald. Using linguistic "psychological signatures," researchers found a landslide match between the play's language and Shakespeare's known works.

French prosecutors denied reports of on-board video footage from the Germanwings Flight 9525 crash site. Meanwhile, Lufthansa confirmed co-pilot Andreas Lubitz had a history of severe depression. Investigators continue to probe the motive behind the fatal crash.

American veteran Emy Afalava and other American Samoans are challenging federal denials of citizenship in a D.C. Circuit lawsuit. The legal action seeks to overturn long-standing precedents that deny residents of U.S. island territories full constitutional rights.

Blue Bell has temporarily shuttered its Broken Arrow, Oklahoma, plant following the discovery of listeria in 3-ounce ice cream servings. The CDC warned consumers against eating specific products from the facility linked to a recent hospital outbreak. Investigations are ongoing to determine if the contamination is the source of recent listeriosis infections.

Al-Shabaab has claimed responsibility for an attack on Garissa University College in eastern Kenya, leaving multiple dead and several hostages. The raid marks an escalation in the group's cross-border activities and highlights deteriorating security in East Africa. Experts suggest the group exploits regional instability and socio-economic exclusion to fuel its militant operations.

The U.S. is filing a diplomatic protest after a Russian SU-27 intercepted a U.S. RC-135U reconnaissance plane over the Baltic Sea. The Pentagon characterized the Russian maneuvers as "unsafe and unprofessional," while Moscow claimed the U.S. aircraft was flying toward its border with its transponder off.

Artist Phillip Hyman created a black-winged angel sculpture to mourn Walter Scott, an unarmed Black man killed by police in North Charleston. The artwork has become a prominent icon for Black Lives Matter protesters during local demonstrations.

Eyewitness video of North Charleston Officer Michael Slager shooting unarmed Walter Scott contradicts initial police reports claiming Scott seized a Taser. Slager has been fired and charged with murder following the incident. Investigations into discrepancies in officer statements and the sequence of events are ongoing.

ISIS claimed to have seized parts of Iraq's Baiji oil refinery following an assault on Saturday. Iraqi government officials denied the militants' claims, maintaining that security forces remain in full control of the facility.

Nashville prosecutors recently banned offering female sterilization as part of plea deals following public outcry. While the practice is legal if voluntarily waived, critics argue it echoes eugenics and disproportionately targets women. The controversy highlights a perceived gender bias in how society views sterilization as a criminal punishment.

More than 25,000 people have contracted Ebola over the past year, resulting in over 10,000 deaths. While weekly infection rates have hit their lowest levels since May 2014, health officials warn that unknown transmission chains in Guinea pose a continued risk.

The NCAA has told a court it has no legal responsibility to ensure the academic integrity of courses offered to student-athletes. The filing responds to a lawsuit from former University of North Carolina athletes alleging academic fraud. Critics argue the stance contradicts the organization's long-standing rhetoric regarding the importance of student education.

An explosion and subsequent fire at a paraxylene plant in Zhangzhou, Fujian province, injured six people Monday night. Authorities say the blast was caused by an oil leak at a storage facility, though no toxic spills have been reported. More than 600 firefighters brought the blaze under control Tuesday morning.

The shooting of Walter Scott by North Charleston police highlights the urgent need for mandatory police body cameras to increase accountability. Proponents argue that body cameras can reduce use-of-force incidents and mitigate the impact of racial bias in law enforcement.

The VII Summit of the Americas faces diplomatic tension as Venezuela's Nicolás Maduro clashes with the U.S. over recent sanctions. While the summit was expected to focus on a historic meeting between Presidents Obama and Castro, Maduro's opposition and support from Cuba have created a "triangle of tension."

A fire broke out on a Russian nuclear submarine undergoing repairs at the Zvyozdochka shipyard. Officials report the blaze was caused by welding work igniting rubber insulation and state that no injuries or radiation threats exist. The vessel is currently empty of ammunition and nuclear fuel.

Philippines authorities warned of flash floods and landslides as tropical storm Maysak approaches the archipelago. The storm is expected to make landfall in Isabela province Sunday morning. Precautionary evacuations and bans on outdoor activities have been implemented in several locales.

Deion Sanders publicly rebuked his son, Deion Sanders Jr., on Twitter after the SMU wide receiver claimed to only eat "hood doughnuts." The NFL legend reminded his son of his wealthy lifestyle, citing his trust fund and luxury assets. Sanders Jr. responded by retweeting the comments.

Guatemala faces an epidemic of gender-based violence and femicide driven by a culture of impunity, machismo, and systemic judicial failure. While survivors and NGOs use art and community programs to challenge social norms, experts warn that international attention is urgently needed to combat the crisis.

Police in Malegaon, India, are requiring cattle owners to submit photographs and detailed physical descriptions of their livestock to create a tracking database. The measure aims to enforce a state-wide ban on beef consumption and cow slaughter following recent criminal cases. Beef traders have protested the crackdown and vowed to challenge the decision in court.

Lucknow police are deploying pepper-spraying drones to control violent protests and mob attacks. The drones, equipped with cameras and spray, have undergone successful testing but face criticism regarding civil liberties and authoritarianism. Official launch of the surveillance measure is expected later this month.
Christie's sold Don McLean's handwritten "American Pie" manuscript for $1.2 million to an unnamed buyer on Tuesday. The 16-page document contains the lyrics to the 1971 folk-rock anthem.

LONDON — Investigators are analyzing the Hatton Garden jewelry heist, a sophisticated vault robbery executed during the Easter weekend. Detectives are focusing on potential inside information and meticulous planning used to bypass security.

7-Eleven will host its first "Bring-Your-Own-Cup Slurpee Day" this Saturday from 11 a.m. to 7 p.m. at participating U.S. stores. Customers may fill any sanitary vessel, such as trophies or sand buckets, for $1.49.

Kentucky State Senator [Name] criticized Rand Paul's presidential campaign announcement, labeling his message of GOP inclusion as "hype." The critic argued Paul's record on civil rights, voting rights, and minority issues contradicts his outreach efforts.

A passenger died Sunday after a Lamborghini crashed into a guardrail during a driving experience at Walt Disney World Speedway. Florida Highway Patrol reported the driver lost control of the vehicle, resulting in one fatality and one minor injury.

Defense attorneys for former NFL player Aaron Hernandez rested their case Monday, concluding their testimony in less than one day. The trial for the alleged murder of Odin Lloyd now moves toward closing arguments and jury deliberations.

Chinese authorities have formally detained feminist activist Wu Rongrong and four others for "creating disturbances" following International Women's Day protests. The detentions come amid a broader crackdown on independent civil society and women's rights activism in China. The activists face potential formal arrest by April 13.

Former Maryland Governor Martin O'Malley challenged Hillary Clinton's perceived inevitability during a speech in Des Moines, Iowa. O'Malley suggested the Democratic primary should feature robust competition rather than a single candidate. Clinton is expected to officially launch her presidential campaign Sunday.

Former NFL player Aaron Hernandez was sentenced to life in prison Wednesday for the first-degree murder of Odin Lloyd. During the sentencing, Lloyd's family provided emotional victim impact statements describing his character and the loss felt since his 2013 death.
Ted Cruz is targeting Iowa's evangelical base to bolster his presidential bid. The senator is leveraging religious themes and social conservative stances to energize voters ahead of the caucuses.

Marvel Studios and other studios released several new character images and details for upcoming superhero films and series. Reveals include Paul Bettany as Vision in "Avengers: Age of Ultron," a first look at the "Daredevil" suit, and Ben Hardy as Angel in "X-Men: Apocalypse." Jamie Bell's portrayal of The Thing in "Fantastic Four" was also unveiled.

Italian Coast Guard rescued 978 migrants from the Mediterranean near Libya on Friday. At least 480 people have died crossing the sea this year due to overcrowding and bad weather. Most migrants originate from West Africa, Somalia, and Syria.

French-language broadcaster TV5Monde is gradually regaining control of its channels and social media following a massive cyberattack. The network reported being hacked by an Islamist group, though no group has officially claimed responsibility.

Director David Lynch has withdrawn from the "Twin Peaks" revival, citing disagreements over production funding. Showtime Network confirmed the third season will proceed without Lynch despite his departure.

High-profile trials for Dzhokhar Tsarnaev and Aaron Hernandez enter critical closing stages in Massachusetts. Meanwhile, Sen. Rand Paul officially launched his presidential bid, and Chicago voters head to the polls for a mayoral runoff. Local elections also proceed in Ferguson, Missouri, amid ongoing racial tensions.

Tornadoes and severe storms swept through Kansas and Missouri on Wednesday night, prompting sirens and reports of wind and flooding damage. Spotters confirmed twister sightings near Goddard, Kansas, and potentially Potosi, Missouri. More storms are forecast for the Midwest and river valleys through Thursday.

Jodi Arias was sentenced to life in prison Monday for the 2008 murder of ex-boyfriend Travis Alexander. The judge denied the possibility of early release after two separate juries deadlocked on the death penalty. Arias will serve her sentence at the Arizona State Prison Complex-Perryville.

The EPA found traces of methyl bromide at a U.S. Virgin Islands luxury villa after a Delaware family was hospitalized with serious illnesses. The Department of Justice has launched a criminal investigation into the incident. Authorities are investigating whether recent pest control services violated environmental regulations.

A Columbia Journalism School review cited "institutional failure" at Rolling Stone regarding its flawed UVA gang rape article. While the university cannot sue for defamation, fraternity members may pursue legal action if they can prove individualized harm and meet specific legal thresholds for group libel.

FBI agents shot and captured Kevone Charleston following a high-speed pursuit and vehicle collisions in Forsyth County, Georgia, on Saturday. Charleston, a suspect in 32 commercial robberies, was wounded during the confrontation. Two federal agents were injured in the crash but have been released from the hospital.

An Alaska Airlines flight from Seattle to Los Angeles made an emergency landing Monday after a ramp agent was discovered asleep in the cargo hold. The contractor, who had fallen asleep during his shift, was unharmed and cleared via drug test. Alaska Airlines is investigating the incident.

A North Carolina judge ruled Monday that Craig Hicks, charged in the fatal shooting of three Muslim college students, faces the possibility of the death penalty. Hicks is indicted on three counts of first-degree murder following the February killings in Chapel Hill. Federal authorities are conducting a parallel inquiry to determine if the shootings constitute a hate crime.

Amnesty International is calling for increased protection for women's rights activists in Afghanistan following a rise in targeted violence. The report highlights systemic failures by authorities to hold perpetrators accountable for attacks on female defenders.

A New York judge has authorized the service of divorce papers via Facebook private messaging. The ruling addresses the difficulty of traditional service when defendants avoid process servers by going "off the grid." Legal experts suggest digital service may be more reliable than antiquated methods like publication or "nail and mail."

Televangelist Robert H. Schuller, founder of "Hour of Power" and the Crystal Cathedral, died Thursday at age 88. Schuller, who battled esophageal cancer, was a pioneer of televised ministry known for his "possibility thinking" message.

Four workers died and 45 were injured in a massive fire at Pemex's Abkatun Permanente oil platform off the Mexican coast Wednesday. Authorities evacuated approximately 300 people as crews battled the blaze in the platform's dehydration and pumping area. Pemex reported the fire is extinguished and denied rumors of a platform collapse or oil spill.

Kansas Governor Sam Brownback signed a first-of-its-kind law banning "dismemberment abortion" procedures. The measure includes an exception to protect the life or health of the mother. Supporters hail the law as a milestone, while opponents condemn it as an extreme restriction on healthcare access.

Chinese state TV host Bi Fujian is under investigation after a video surfaced showing him cursing the late Chairman Mao Zedong during a dinner party. Bi issued a public apology for the "grave social consequences" of his remarks. CCTV has confirmed it will investigate the incident.

Kentucky guard Andrew Harrison issued an apology after a hot mic captured him using a racial slur toward Wisconsin's Frank Kaminsky following a loss. Harrison stated the remark was made "in jest" and has since spoken with Kaminsky to apologize. Kaminsky said he has moved past the incident.
Executive producer Brian Grazer announced "Arrested Development" will return for a 17-episode fifth season. Netflix has not yet verified the news. Cast involvement remains unconfirmed.

CERN has successfully restarted the Large Hadron Collider (LHC) following a two-year shutdown. The particle accelerator aims to replicate Big Bang conditions to study dark matter and the origins of the universe. Scientists plan to increase beam energy to record levels in upcoming phases.

An Iranian observation aircraft flew within 50 yards of a U.S. Navy helicopter over the Persian Gulf this month. U.S. officials suspect the unsafe maneuver was ordered by a local commander rather than Tehran leadership. The administration is considering a formal protest regarding the incident.
A jury found Dzhokhar Tsarnaev guilty on all 30 counts related to the Boston Marathon bombing. The trial will now proceed to a penalty phase to determine if Tsarnaev will face the death penalty.

Police arrested four FabIndia employees in Goa after Minister Smriti Irani discovered a surveillance camera overlooking a store changing room. Authorities confirmed the camera was capable of photographing customers, leading to charges of voyeurism and breach of privacy. The store has been sealed as investigations continue.

Iran plans to lift bans on women and families attending certain indoor sporting events within the next year, according to Deputy Sports Minister Abdolhamid Ahmadi. The policy change follows international pressure to end decades-old restrictions on women attending men's sports. Specific details regarding which matches will be accessible remain unconfirmed.

Former Satyam Computers chairman Ramalinga Raju and nine others have been sentenced to seven years in prison for their roles in a $1.6 billion fraud scandal. A special court convicted the group of cheating and criminal conspiracy involving inflated profits and fictitious assets. Raju was also ordered to pay a fine of $804,000.

Alaska Airlines apologized and issued refunds after removing a passenger from a flight to Hawaii due to her cancer diagnosis. The airline cited safety protocols regarding medical issues, but admitted the situation was handled poorly.

Turkish singer and songwriter Kayahan died of cancer in Istanbul on Friday at age 66. The former Eurovision contestant was a prominent figure in Turkish music, best known for his prolific career of love songs and nearly 20 albums.

Israeli PM Benjamin Netanyahu criticized the proposed Iran nuclear deal as a "bad deal," advocating for increased pressure to secure better terms. U.S. lawmakers remain divided, with Republicans calling for more stringent options and Democrats defending the framework as a workable opportunity.

A series of connected shootings involving a suspected kidnapping left a security guard and a police officer wounded in the Washington area. The incident began at the U.S. Census Bureau headquarters and ended following a vehicle chase and shootout on H Street. The kidnapping victim was located and is reported to be in good condition.
Imprisoned whistleblower Chelsea Manning has joined Twitter via a third-party firm. The former Army analyst will dictate messages to bypass prison internet restrictions.

Rapper Nelly was arrested in Tennessee Saturday following a bus inspection that uncovered methamphetamine, marijuana, and drug paraphernalia. Authorities also seized several handguns and packaging materials during the search. Nelly has since posted bond and been released from custody.

A Delaware family fell ill in the U.S. Virgin Islands after potentially being exposed to methyl bromide at a rental villa. The EPA found traces of the restricted pesticide in the unit, prompting a criminal investigation by the Department of Justice. Two boys remain in critical condition while their father is in stable condition.

Online bloggers and activists in Asia face increasing risks of imprisonment and violence as governments crack down on digital dissent. Authorities in countries like Singapore, Malaysia, and Vietnam use legal and financial pressure to silence online voices. In regions with weak rule of law, such as Bangladesh, bloggers face lethal attacks from militants with near-total impunity.

Nina Dobrev announced she will depart "Vampire Diaries" at the end of the current season. Fans expressed outrage on social media, questioning the show's future following her exit. Producers confirmed they will continue the series next fall without the actress.

Yarmouk refugee camp faces escalating destruction as ISIS and government forces engage in intense urban combat. Besieged residents report severe shortages of food, water, and medical supplies amid ongoing shelling. UNRWA officials warn that international aid remains insufficient to reach the trapped civilian population.

NASA scientists outline strategies for detecting extraterrestrial life over the next two decades using advanced telescopes and planetary atmosphere analysis. While astronomers estimate billions of Earth-like planets exist in the Milky Way, the likelihood of encountering communicative, intelligent civilizations remains extremely low. Future missions will focus on identifying biological signatures on rocky exoplanets and exploring water-rich moons in our solar system.

Massachusetts man Carlos Colina, 32, faces murder charges following the discovery of human remains in a duffel bag and apartment building in Cambridge. Authorities identified the victim as 26-year-old Jonathan Camilien, an acquaintance of Colina. Colina is scheduled for arraignment on April 14.

Kanye West has settled a civil lawsuit with photographer Daniel Ramos following a 2013 battery incident at Los Angeles International Airport. Ramos' attorney confirmed the case was dismissed after an undisclosed settlement and a formal apology from West.

Obama's pursuit of an Iran nuclear deal is being driven by political legacy rather than strategic necessity, weakening U.S. leverage. The proposed framework allows Iran to maintain significant nuclear infrastructure and risks regional instability by lifting sanctions too early. Critics argue the deal fails to prevent Iran from becoming a nuclear threshold state.

The killing of Walter Scott by a South Carolina police officer highlights a critical lack of national data on police use of force. Despite a 1994 federal law, the Justice Department has failed to implement mandatory data collection, leaving the scale of police violence unrecorded. Advocates are calling for increased pressure on Washington to enforce transparency and end the systemic withholding of information.
Five Americans exposed to Ebola in Sierra Leone have been released from an Omaha hospital after three weeks of monitoring. None of the clinicians developed the virus.

Mark Ronson's "Uptown Funk!" featuring Bruno Mars has spent 13 weeks at No. 1 on the Billboard Hot 100, becoming the longest-leading single of the 2010s. The track joins an elite group of only 10 songs in chart history to hold the top spot for at least 13 weeks. Natalie La Rose's debut single "Somebody" also entered the top 10.

April 8 marked "Rex Manning Day" from the film "Empire Records," alongside other significant pop culture dates. Notable upcoming film anniversaries include "Titanic" on April 14, "Miss Congeniality" on April 25, and "Mean Girls" on October 3. "Back to the Future Part II" also highlights October 21, 2015, as a key cinematic date.

Lifetime will premiere "Grace of Monaco," starring Nicole Kidman, on May 25. The Weinstein Co. opted to sell the film directly to the network following poor international performance and a scrapped theatrical release.

Shibuya ward in Tokyo has passed an ordinance to issue partnership certificates to same-sex couples. The measure grants limited rights, such as hospital visitation and tenancy co-signing, but does not equate to legal marriage. Proponents call the move a significant step toward marriage equality in Japan.

Persistent drought in California and the Southwest is driving up national food prices, specifically for fruits, vegetables, and beef. Governor Jerry Brown has mandated a 25% water cutback in all cities as the crisis impacts agricultural production and livestock grazing. While a strong dollar and lower oil prices may mitigate some costs, experts warn of continued volatility in supermarket prices.

University of Michigan will proceed with a screening of "American Sniper" despite student protests over its depiction of the Iraq War. Officials reversed an initial cancellation, citing the importance of freedom of expression.

The 2015 MTV Movie Awards featured standout moments from host Amy Schumer and a twerking performance by Channing Tatum. The broadcast included musical sets from Fall Out Boy and Fetty Wap, alongside various comedic highlights and technical misfires.

A 20-to-30-foot fiberglass boat fragment, suspected to be debris from the 2011 Japan earthquake and tsunami, was recovered off the Oregon coast. The debris contained several Japanese yellowtail jack fish, which will be transferred to the Oregon Coast Aquarium for study.

One year after Boko Haram militants abducted 276 schoolgirls from Chibok, Nigeria, most of the victims remain missing. President-elect Muhammadu Buhari and global activists marked the anniversary by calling for action against the terrorist group. The kidnapping continues to fuel international outrage and the trending #BringBackOurGirls campaign.

The Easter Triduum—comprising Good Friday, Holy Saturday, and Easter Sunday—serves as a spiritual progression from suffering to transformation. The three-day cycle mirrors the universal human experience of navigating darkness, transition, and eventual renewal.

Kenya has frozen 86 bank accounts linked to suspected Al-Shabaab supporters following a university massacre that killed 147 people. Authorities are also offering a reward for information on the alleged organizer of the attack. The crackdown follows intense public criticism regarding the government's response to the Garissa siege.

Entrepreneur Jia Jiang releases "Rejection Proof," a book detailing his "100 Days of Rejection" project designed to overcome the fear of failure. The project, which gained viral fame, aims to teach individuals how to transform rejection into opportunity.

Attorney General Eric Holder issued a memo prohibiting all Justice Department personnel from soliciting or accepting commercial sex, regardless of local legality. The directive follows reports of misconduct involving DEA agents and aims to combat human trafficking. Violators face suspension or termination, even when off duty.

Authorities are investigating the fatal shooting of a Wayne Community College employee as a potential hate crime. Suspect Kenneth Morgan Stancil III was arrested on a Florida beach after fleeing the North Carolina crime scene.

Amnesty International reports a global spike in death sentences as governments use capital punishment to combat terrorism and crime. Despite rising political use of executions, total global executions fell from 778 to 607 in 2014.

A Duke University student admitted to hanging a noose near a student union on Wednesday. The student has been removed from campus pending a conduct review and ongoing criminal investigations. Hundreds of students and faculty held a protest following the incident.
Emmy-winning actor Richard Dysart has died at age 86 following a long illness. Dysart was best known for his role as Leland McKenzie on the NBC drama "L.A. Law."

Easter celebrations mark the Christian commemoration of Christ's resurrection, with Pope Francis delivering an Urbi et Orbi address amid global conflict. The holiday's shifting date is determined by lunar cycles and the vernal equinox, often resulting in different celebration dates for Western and Orthodox Christians. Traditional customs like Easter bunnies and eggs have roots in German immigrant history and seasonal agricultural practices.

Comedian Chris Rock sparked social media debate after tweeting about multiple recent traffic stops. The posts highlight ongoing racial disparities in policing and "driving while black" concerns. Some users praised the documentation, while others criticized suggestions to change behavior to avoid profiling.
Original Lynyrd Skynyrd drummer Robert Lewis Burns Jr. died Friday night in a single-vehicle car crash in Cartersville, Georgia. Burns, 64, struck a mailbox and a tree shortly before midnight.
An optical illusion photo of a cat on stairs has gone viral on social media. Users are debating whether the animal is moving up or down the steps.

The U.S. and P5+1 partners reached a framework agreement with Iran in Switzerland to limit its nuclear program and prevent weapon development. The deal includes reduced uranium stockpiles and permanent IAEA inspection access, despite anticipated political opposition in Congress.

University of Virginia faces ongoing investigations into its handling of sexual assault following a retracted Rolling Stone article. While the magazine's central narrative was discredited, the report highlighted systemic issues regarding campus culture and the university's failure to expel students for sexual violence.

Indiana Pacers player Chris Copeland was hospitalized in stable condition after being stabbed outside a New York City nightclub early Wednesday. A suspect is in custody, while Atlanta Hawks players Pero Antic and Thabo Sefolosha were arrested on obstruction and disorderly conduct charges during the incident.

Twisted Sister has announced its 2016 "Forty and F*ck It" tour will be the band's final run. The farewell tour marks the group's 40th anniversary and features new drummer Mike Portnoy. The band will also perform two tribute shows for late drummer A.J. Pero.

Actor John Travolta dismissed HBO's critical Scientology documentary "Going Clear," stating he has no interest in watching the film. Travolta defended his 40-year involvement with the Church, attributing his personal resilience to the organization.

"Furious 7" earned a record $146 million opening weekend, drawing emotional reactions from fans regarding its tribute to late actor Paul Walker. Filmmakers used body doubles and CGI to complete the film, opting to retire Walker's character rather than kill him off.

HBO's "Game of Thrones" fifth season premieres Sunday in 170 countries, marking a major expansion of the series' global reach. Executive producers promise larger battles and intensifying drama as key story arcs converge. Experts suggest the season will see major characters move ahead of the original book source material.

Survivors of extreme maritime accidents have recounted harrowing tales of endurance after being lost at sea for days or months. Recent cases include individuals surviving on rainwater and raw fish, with one man drifting for over a year in the Pacific.
The first six "Star Wars" films will be released on digital HD this Friday. The collection includes special features, such as a behind-the-scenes look at the creation of Geonosian sound effects.

Dzhokhar Tsarnaev found guilty on all 30 counts related to the 2013 Boston Marathon bombings. The verdict provides accountability for the deadly attacks and their aftermath. Survivors and victims' families expressed a mix of relief and grief following the decision.

China's state prosecutors have formally charged former security czar Zhou Yongkang with bribery, abuse of power, and leaking state secrets. As a former member of the Politburo Standing Committee, Zhou is the highest-ranking official ever to face such corruption charges. The case marks a major milestone in President Xi Jinping's ongoing anti-corruption campaign.

A Philadelphia woman faces multiple felony charges after allegedly abandoning her 21-year-old quadriplegic son in a park for four days to visit a boyfriend in Maryland. The victim was found suffering from dehydration, malnutrition, and infection. Police have taken the mother into custody in Maryland pending extradition.

Walmart's opposition to an Arkansas religious freedom bill has prompted the governor to delay signing the legislation. The retailer's stance reflects a broader trend of major corporations pushing for LGBTQ+ nondiscrimination protections. Analysts suggest the company's shift signals changing public opinion and potential political realignment for the GOP.

A lapsed Catholic describes how Pope Francis's inclusive approach and emphasis on compassion have reawakened their faith. The author cites the Pope's non-judgmental tone regarding social issues and his focus on the Gospel as key drivers for this spiritual reconnection.

Mary Kay Letourneau and husband Vili Fualaau will appear in an exclusive ABC "20/20" interview to discuss their marriage and upcoming 10th anniversary. The couple, whose 1996 affair led to Letourneau's imprisonment, will address their relationship, Letourneau's teaching ambitions, and Fualaau's personal struggles.

Hillary Clinton's presidential candidacy serves as a high-stakes litmus test for gender equality in the United States. While her campaign faces unique scrutiny regarding sexism, electoral outcomes will likely be driven more by partisanship and the economy than by gender.

Amnesty International reports that governments are using terrorism threats to justify executions, despite a 22% global decrease in total executions in 2014. However, the report notes a 28% spike in death sentences worldwide, driven by mass sentencing in countries like Egypt and Nigeria.

Japan Defense Minister Gen Nakatani told parliament that the Air Self Defense Force has never encountered extraterrestrial unidentified flying objects. The statement followed questioning by lawmaker Antonio Inoki regarding whether fighter jets are scrambled to meet potential alien threats.

Mark Wahlberg will star in and produce "Patriots' Day," a film about the Boston Marathon bombing told from the perspective of Police Commissioner Ed Davis. Produced by CBS Films using "60 Minutes" research, the project follows Fox's previously announced film "Boston Strong."

DES MOINES, Iowa — Potential presidential contenders Martin O'Malley and Jim Webb shared a stage at a Democratic awards dinner Friday, showcasing contrasting political styles. O'Malley engaged in active retail politics while Webb maintained a more stoic, subdued presence. Both candidates face long odds in a field currently dominated by Hillary Clinton.

Turkish authorities arrested nine British citizens, including four children, at the Turkey-Syria border on Wednesday. The group is suspected of attempting to enter Syria illegally. The UK Foreign Office is currently seeking information from Turkish officials regarding the incident.

The U.S. Department of Justice has filed a 15-count indictment against FedEx, alleging the company conspired to transport illegal prescription drugs and engaged in money laundering. FedEx maintains its innocence, citing "common carrier" protections that shield couriers from liability for the contents of packages. The prosecution argues FedEx ignored warnings regarding illegal internet pharmacies and suspicious drug distribution activities.

Kenyans used social media to honor victims of the Al-Shabaab terrorist attack at Garissa University College, which killed 147 people. The massacre, Kenya's deadliest since 1998, has prompted nationwide mourning and heightened security during Easter services. Authorities identified one attacker as the son of a government official.

Photographer Johan Bavman is documenting Swedish fathers utilizing the nation's extensive parental leave system through a new photo project. Despite government incentives to promote gender equality, Bavman notes that most men still prioritize careers over full leave. The project aims to highlight the realistic bonding and challenges experienced by men taking extended time off to care for newborns.

President Obama pledged to ensure Israel maintains a qualitative military advantage despite criticism of the Iran nuclear deal. Obama stated the U.S. would stand by Israel against state attacks to provide security while pursuing a framework to halt Tehran's nuclear ambitions.

U.S. religious freedom laws face scrutiny as states like Indiana use them to potentially permit discrimination. While federal and state statutes aim to protect religious practices, legal battles over sacred items, substances, and dietary needs show inconsistent application. Experts note that successful claims under these laws are rare and often benefit religious minorities rather than major denominations.

Five Chinese feminist activists face up to five years in prison following charges of "assembling a crowd to disturb public order." The women were detained in March for planning International Women's Day protests against sexual harassment. The detentions have drawn international condemnation from human rights groups and political figures.

The family of late Tejano singer Selena is partnering with Acrovirt LLC to create "Selena the One," a digital embodiment capable of singing, dancing, and interacting. The project aims to expand her legacy through new music, collaborations, and a planned 2018 tour. An Indiegogo campaign to fund the technology launch begins April 16.

Former Rep. Michele Bachmann drew intense criticism after comparing President Obama to the Germanwings co-pilot accused of a fatal plane crash. Bachmann likened Obama's Iran nuclear deal to a "deranged pilot" flying the nation into destruction. Critics labeled the Facebook comments "despicable" and "inappropriate."

Ryan Gosling’s directorial debut "Lost River" begins limited theatrical release in the U.S. and UK on April 10. The divisive film uses the decaying landscape of Detroit as a central character to explore themes of urban destruction and community resilience. Gosling stated the project was inspired by the need to document the city's crumbling architecture before its demolition.

A 19-year-old UK national, Yahya Rashid, has been charged with terror offenses following his arrest at Luton airport. Rashid faces charges of preparing for terrorism and assisting others in committing terrorist acts. He is scheduled to appear in Westminster Magistrates' Court on Wednesday.

Performances of the American national anthem range from legendary to disastrous. High-profile singers such as Whitney Houston and Jimi Hendrix have set standards, while others like Roseanne Barr and Vince Neil have faced significant criticism.

Photographer Jeff Gusky has uncovered nearly 2,000 pieces of WWI-era graffiti inside a vast underground chalk quarry near Naours, France. The inscriptions, left by Allied soldiers seeking refuge from battle, provide a rare human connection to the conflict. Local authorities are working to preserve the site to promote historical awareness.

The Palestinian Authority officially became the 123rd member of the International Criminal Court on Wednesday, granting the court jurisdiction over alleged crimes in Palestinian territories. The move, welcomed by human rights groups, faces strong opposition from Israel and the United States. The ICC's preliminary examination into the region could lead to war crimes investigations against both Israeli and Palestinian actors.

Anthony Ray Hinton was released from an Alabama death row Friday after serving nearly 30 years for murders he did not commit. A judge ordered his release after the state declined to re-prosecute the case following evidence that the murder weapon could not be linked to the crimes. Hinton's legal team cited prosecutorial indifference and systemic injustice as factors in the decades-long wrongful conviction.

Most Americans view tax season positively due to large average refunds and simplified filing processes. However, critics argue these "happy endings" mask systemic inequities, including a bias toward capital gains over wages and penalties for dual-income marriages.

Jordan Spieth holds a four-shot lead heading into the final round of the Masters after a steady third round. Phil Mickelson and Justin Rose sit in second place, while Tiger Woods and Rory McIlroy finished six under par.

A Bronx woman faces criminal charges for allegedly participating in an immigration scam involving 10 marriages. Prosecutors say Barrientos filed false marriage licenses to help husbands obtain permanent residency. She pleaded not guilty to felony counts of offering a false instrument for filing.

An Indiana pizzeria facing boycotts and threats after refusing to cater a same-sex wedding has received over $842,000 in donations from supporters. The controversy stems from the owners' stance on the state's Religious Freedom Restoration Act. Local police are investigating online threats against the business.

Vijay Chokalingam, brother of comedian Mindy Kaling, is planning a book about posing as African-American to gain admission to medical schools. Chokalingam claims the deception was intended to expose unfair advantages in affirmative action policies. Critics note he received only one admission offer and faced increased racial profiling during his experiment.

Antarctica recorded a potential record high of 63.5 degrees Fahrenheit at Argentina's Esperanza Base on March 24. The World Meteorological Organization is forming a committee of climatologists to investigate the measurement's accuracy. Official findings are expected by late summer or early fall.

U.S. officials say there is no set timeframe for an Iraqi-led offensive to retake Mosul from ISIS. While airstrikes continue in the region, administration officials stressed that building necessary military capacity will take time.

Paddy Power has deleted a controversial tweet comparing Newcastle United's losses to the killing of unarmed African-American men by police. The betting company issued an apology, stating the post was intended as a joke, but faced widespread condemnation on social media.

Philadelphia police added attempted murder to the charges against Nyia Parler, who allegedly abandoned her quadriplegic son in a park for four days. Parler is currently in custody in Maryland for unspecified treatment and awaits extradition.

South Korean authorities have charged Kim Ki-Jong with attempted murder, assault, and business obstruction following the March 5 stabbing of U.S. Ambassador Mark Lippert in Seoul. Kim, who opposed joint military drills, faces trial within 14 days. Investigators are looking into the suspect's previous visits to North Korea.
Jill Dillard, the first daughter from TLC's "19 Kids and Counting" to marry, has given birth to a son, Israel David. The 9-pound, 10-ounce baby arrived Monday, more than a week past his due date.

Universal's "Furious 7" is projected to debut domestically between $135 million and $138 million, marking the largest North American opening since fall 2013. The film's global debut could approach $300 million following a record-breaking $60 million international start. The release marks Universal's widest distribution to date.

A Secret Service supervisor has been placed on administrative leave following allegations of sexual assault against a female employee. The incident, involving unwanted advances and a physical struggle, follows a series of recent security lapses and scandals at the agency. An investigation by the Office of the Inspector General is ongoing.

Hillary Clinton has announced her candidacy for the 2016 presidential election, leveraging extensive political experience to bolster Democratic prospects. To succeed, she must overcome challenges regarding authenticity, connect with the party base, and manage potential liabilities involving her husband.

The Department of Justice will begin negotiations to restructure the Ferguson police department following findings of systemic racial discrimination and predatory municipal practices. Recent local elections have shifted the city council's racial composition, signaling a leadership transition alongside the resignations of the town manager and police chief. The scope of future reforms remains dependent on upcoming DOJ negotiations and continued community activism.

Etihad Airways is investigating the disappearance of a 2-year-old cat, Felix, after the pet's carrier was found crushed following a flight from Abu Dhabi to New York. The owners allege the animal escaped at JFK International Airport due to damaged equipment. Search efforts involving detection dogs and traps are currently underway.

LOUIS JORDAN, 37, was rescued Thursday after drifting at sea for 66 days in a damaged sailboat. Jordan survived by catching fish with laundry and collecting rainwater despite multiple storms and a broken shoulder. He was spotted and rescued by the crew of the container ship Houston Express.
